keyFindings.finding: Fossil fuel combustion is the dominant driver of climate change, accounting for approximately 75% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions
Agricultural emissions contribute 24% of global emissions through methane from livestock (14.5% alone) and nitrous oxide from fertilizers
Deforestation and land use change contribute 10-15% of global emissions while simultaneously reducing carbon sequestration capacity
Industrial process emissions, particularly from cement production (8% of global CO2), represent emissions beyond energy use that are inherent to manufacturing processes
Different greenhouse gases have vastly different warming potentials: methane is 80x more potent than CO2 over 20 years, nitrous oxide is 300x more potent
Climate feedback mechanisms amplify initial warming through processes like ice-albedo feedback, permafrost thaw, and ocean CO2 release
Multiple lines of evidence including isotopic signatures, spatial patterns, and attribution studies definitively establish anthropogenic causation of current warming
Transportation sector accounts for 16% of global emissions, with road vehicles as the primary contributor
